canonical_statement: The GUSTO IIa trial was initiated to compare intravenous heparin with recombinant hirudin in patients with acute coronary syndromes in a randomized, double-blind, multinational trial.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we initiated a randomized, double-blind, multinational trial of heparin compared with recombinant hirudin

canonical_statement: Eligible patients were within 12 hours of chest discomfort onset and had an abnormal ECG with qualifying ST-segment deviation or T-wave inversion.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: patients had to be <12 hours from the onset of chest discomfort and to present with an abnormal ECG

population.label: Patients screened for GUSTO IIa
inclusion_criteria: ST elevation or depression >=0.05 mV or T-wave inversion >=0.1 mV

canonical_statement: Patients with active bleeding, serum creatinine greater than 2.5 mg/dL, stroke within the prior year, or a contraindication to heparin were excluded.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients with active bleeding, a serum creatinine >2.5 mg/dL, prior stroke within 1 year, or contraindication to heparin were excluded.

canonical_statement: Patients were stratified by ST-segment elevation; those with qualifying ST elevation were eligible for accelerated tissue-type plasminogen activator or streptokinase.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: patients were stratified into two groups: those with ST-segment elevation

population.label: GUSTO IIa randomized acute coronary syndrome population

exposures.details: Accelerated tissue-type plasminogen activator or streptokinase for eligible ST-elevation patients

canonical_statement: The heparin regimen used a 5000-unit intravenous bolus followed by 1000 units/hour for patients under 80 kg or 1300 units/hour for patients at least 80 kg; the infusion continued 72 to 120 hours and was adjusted to an aPTT of 60 to 90 seconds.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the dose was a 5000-U bolus followed by 1000 U per hour for patients weighing <80 kg and 1300 U per hour for patients >=80 kg

exposures.details: 5000-U bolus; infusion 1000 U/h if <80 kg or 1300 U/h if >=80 kg; aPTT target 60-90 s

canonical_statement: The recombinant desulfatohirudin regimen used a 0.6-mg/kg intravenous bolus followed by 0.2 mg/kg/hour for 72 to 120 hours, without routine aPTT adjustment unless aPTT exceeded 150 seconds.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The dose of hirudin ... was a 0.6-mg/kg bolus and 0.2 mg/kg per hour

exposures.details: 0.6 mg/kg bolus; 0.2 mg/kg/h infusion; no adjustment unless aPTT >150 s

canonical_statement: A double-infusion-bag design was used to preserve double blinding of patients and investigators.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Both infusions were maintained for 72 to 120 hours with a double-infusion bag to preserve a double-blind status

canonical_statement: aPTT was measured at 6, 12, and 24 hours and then at least daily during antithrombin therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The aPTT was serially measured at 6, 12, and 24 hours, and then at least once a day.

canonical_statement: The prespecified primary efficacy endpoint was death or myocardial infarction within 30 days.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The primary end point was death or MI within 30 days.

canonical_statement: Intracranial hemorrhage was defined as an acute new neurologic deficit causing death or lasting more than 24 hours, with neurologist classification and imaging or autopsy evidence of hemorrhage.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Intracranial hemorrhage was defined as an acute new neurological deficit resulting in death or lasting >24 hours

outcome.definition: Acute new neurologic deficit resulting in death or lasting >24 h, classified by a neurologist, with CT, MRI, or autopsy demonstrating hemorrhage

canonical_statement: Deaths, strokes, and myocardial infarctions were reviewed by an independent adjudication committee blinded to treatment assignment.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All events of death, stroke, and MI were reviewed by an independent adjudication committee blinded to therapy assignment.

canonical_statement: The planned sample size was 12,000 patients, assuming an 8.5% overall event rate and a 20% reduction with recombinant hirudin, with alpha 0.025 and beta 0.10.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The trial's sample size was calculated to be 12 000 patients

canonical_statement: A data and safety monitoring committee was convened to review data after the first 1,000 patients and provide ongoing surveillance for bleeding events.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A data and safety monitoring committee was convened to review the data after the first 1000 patients were entered

canonical_statement: This report presented only intracranial hemorrhage outcome data; final efficacy and detailed secondary outcomes were deferred, and most baseline, treatment, and outcome data were described as preliminary pending quality control.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Only the intracranial hemorrhage outcome data are included in this report. Final efficacy data ... will be the subject of a future report.

canonical_statement: The trial was terminated early on April 8, 1994 because of an excess of intracerebral hemorrhage after 2,564 patients had been enrolled.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: terminated earlier than planned on April 8, 1994, because of an excess of intracerebral hemorrhage

canonical_statement: Compared with the GUSTO I intravenous-heparin reference cohort, the GUSTO IIa cohort was older and included a greater proportion of women; weight did not differ significantly.

population.label: GUSTO IIa cohort compared with GUSTO I intravenous-heparin reference cohort

canonical_statement: Overall hemorrhagic stroke occurred in 17 of 1,273 hirudin patients (1.3%; 95% CI 0.7%-2.0%) and 9 of 1,291 heparin patients (0.7%; 95% CI 0.2%-1.2%); P=.11.
Hemorrhagic stroke occurred in 1.8% of 1,264 patients receiving thrombolytic therapy versus 0.3% of 1,168 patients not receiving thrombolytics; P<.001.

canonical_statement: At 12 hours, patients who developed hemorrhagic stroke had a mean aPTT of 110±46 seconds compared with 87±36 seconds in patients without hemorrhagic stroke; P=.031.

canonical_statement: At least two hemorrhagic strokes occurred in the setting of renal dysfunction.

canonical_statement: At the hirudin dose tested, the authors concluded there was a trend toward excess hemorrhagic stroke compared with heparin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: At the dose of hirudin tested, there was a trend of an excess of hemorrhagic stroke compared with heparin.

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that the approximately 20% higher heparin dose used in GUSTO IIa versus GUSTO I was accompanied by about a twofold hemorrhagic-stroke risk in thrombolytic-treated patients.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Heparin, at a slightly higher dose than previously used ... was accompanied by a twofold risk of hemorrhagic stroke

canonical_statement: The authors concluded that aPTT appeared useful for predicting hemorrhagic-stroke risk with both heparin and hirudin in patients receiving thrombolytic therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: With both thrombin inhibitors, the aPTT appears to be a useful index for predicting risk of hemorrhagic stroke

canonical_statement: The authors interpreted the safety findings as highlighting a very narrow therapeutic window for heparin when used with thrombolytic therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: these data highlight a very narrow therapeutic window for heparin administration with thrombolytic therapy.

canonical_statement: The authors recommended serial aPTT monitoring during antithrombin therapy because upward deviation from the 60- to 85-second target range was linked with higher catastrophic hemorrhage risk, while noting uncertainty about the preferred range and assay variability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: serial monitoring of the aPTT value appears to be warranted during antithrombin therapy

canonical_statement: The authors stated that hirudin should be monitored and titrated similarly to heparin and that concern is warranted when aPTT exceeds 100 seconds.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: indicate a need to monitor and titrate hirudin therapy ... and to be concerned when the aPTT level exceeds 100 seconds.

canonical_statement: The increased intracerebral hemorrhage rate with streptokinase plus either heparin or hirudin was considered to warrant further study of the need for and risk of conjunctive antithrombin therapy with streptokinase.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the increased rate of intracerebral hemorrhage with streptokinase and heparin or hirudin ... raises the issue of need for and risk of conjunctive antithrombin therapy

canonical_statement: After the safety findings, the trial was reinitiated with lower doses: heparin returned to the GUSTO I regimen, hirudin was reduced to a 0.1-mg/kg bolus plus 0.1 mg/kg/hour, and the aPTT target was reduced to 60 to 85 seconds with down-titration for marked prolongation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the trial has been re-initiated at lower doses of heparin ... and hirudin (0.1-mg/kg bolus and 0.1-mg/kg per hour infusion)

canonical_statement: The reinitiated trial added exclusion of prior stroke and uncontrolled hypertension (systolic blood pressure >200 mm Hg), lowered the serum creatinine exclusion threshold to >2.0 mg/dL, and increased attention to renal dysfunction during therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we have added the exclusion of prior stroke and uncontrolled hypertension ... exclusion of patients with creatinine >2.0 mg/dL

canonical_statement: The authors noted uncertainty about whether the higher-risk GUSTO IIa population, which included older patients and more women than the prior trial, partly accounted for the excessive hemorrhagic risk.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: it remains uncertain whether the higher risk population, with older patients and more women, may at least in part have accounted for the excessive risk

canonical_statement: The authors emphasized that safety studies should follow and complement angiographic studies when evaluating intensive antithrombotic therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Our findings emphasize the importance of safety studies following and complementing angiographic studies.
